planting.note: Direct sow in cool weather and succession sow every one to two weeks for continuous harvest; Zlata's golden-yellow skin makes it stand out easily from red radishes in a mixed planting.

directions: Sow seed directly half an inch deep in cool, moist soil and thin to about an inch apart for well-formed roots. Zlata is a round, golden-yellow-skinned radish with crisp white flesh and a mild flavor, notably slower to turn pithy or overly hot than many red radishes when the weather warms, which extends its harvest window into the edge of the cool season. The bright yellow skin adds welcome color contrast to salads, radish plates, and pickles alongside standard red and white types. Harvest promptly once roots reach about an inch across, and keep soil consistently moist through growth, since inconsistent watering causes cracked or overly pungent roots.

common_name: Munich Bier Radish (German Beer Garden Radish)

planting.note: Direct sow in cool weather; Munich Bier grows considerably larger than salad radishes and needs a bit more room and time to size up, so thin seedlings generously.

directions: Sow seed directly half an inch deep in fertile, well-drained soil and thin to a few inches apart, since this variety forms a substantially larger root than typical salad radishes. Munich Bier is an old German heirloom traditionally served whole, sliced, or spiraled and lightly salted as a salty, crunchy snack alongside beer in Bavarian beer gardens, a use quite different from the quick-growing salad radishes most American gardeners know. Its large white roots stay crisp and mild-flavored even at full size, resisting the pithiness and heat that ruins many radishes left in the ground too long. Harvest once roots reach 3-4 inches across, and keep soil evenly moist throughout growth for the best crisp, mild-flavored roots.
